About the ghosts in Photos.app: the bytes are off your phone, but Photos.app still has database entries that point to the now-missing files. They show up as photos with a small ! badge and "unable to load higher quality version".

To clean them up: open Photos > Library > All Photos on your iPhone > tap any ghost > Select > Select All > Trash > then open Albums > Recently Deleted > Select > Delete All. Yes, it's two steps. We're working on automating it (see issue #1 — one Touch ID on the Mac).

Wring it dry?

        
After every file is safely written to disk, DumpSock will
          remove it from /var/mobile/Media/DCIM/ on your
          iPhone over USB. Storage is freed immediately.

        
Only the files actually written to your chosen
          output folder will be removed. Files that fail to transfer,
          or whose size doesn't verify, are never deleted.

        
Photos.app will show ghost entries for the
          removed files. To clean those: select them in Photos.app and
          delete them, then empty Recently Deleted. We're automating
          that one-Touch-ID flow next (see issue #1).
